blogs.title: Exemption 7(A) in the Age of Counterterrorism: Why the D.C. Circuit Still Defers to the FBI
blogs.description: This post will dissect the court’s heavy deference to the FBI’s judgment that the Farahi records were compiled for law‑enforcement purposes. It will trace the doctrinal lineage of deference in FOIA cases, evaluate the balance between executive expertise and judicial oversight, and consider whether the D.C. Circuit’s reliance on agency expertise—especially in national‑security investigations—risks eroding the statutory mandate for transparency.

blogs.title: Pending or Anticipated? The Elusive Standard for “Interference” Under FOIA Exemption 7(A)
blogs.description: The opinion leans on the “pending or reasonably anticipated” test to uphold the FBI’s claim that disclosure would interfere with enforcement. This article will analyze how the court interpreted that test, how it reconciles the passage of time with ongoing investigations, and what the decision means for future FOIA litigants who argue that an investigation has effectively ended.

blogs.title: Segregability After the Fact: When ‘Inextricably Intertwined’ Becomes a Catch‑All
blogs.description: Focusing on the court’s finding that no reasonably segregable material existed in Farahi’s 10,750‑page file, this piece will explore the legal standards for segregation, the burden on agencies to justify non‑segregability, and the practical implications for plaintiffs seeking even a sliver of non‑exempt information from massive, classified dossiers.

blogs.title: Ex Parte Declarations and FOIA: A Double‑Edged Sword for Transparency
blogs.description: The ruling relied heavily on sealed, ex‑parte declarations from FBI officials. This blog will examine the tension between protecting sensitive investigative details and the plaintiff’s right to contest the basis of withholding. It will assess the D.C. Circuit’s view that such declarations are permissible, discuss the procedural safeguards (or lack thereof), and suggest reforms to ensure fairer FOIA litigation.
